 Asset Description : 
 A centrifugal fan, also known as an axial fan, is a type of fan that uses an impeller to convert rotational kinetic energy into thrust. The main components of a centrifugal fan include the inlet box, inlet screen or grille, damper or inlet vanes, fan blades, speed changer, lubrication system, oil coolers, housing, bearing pedestals, and foundation. The inlet box is the entry point for the air, and may include a filter or screen to remove debris. The inlet vanes or dampers are used to control the airflow into the fan. The fan blades are the curved surfaces that direct the airflow. The speed changer is used to adjust the rotational speed of the fan. The lubrication system is used to provide lubrication to the moving parts of the fan. The oil coolers are used to remove heat from the lubrication system. The housing is the outer casing of the fan, and the bearing pedestals support the fan blades and provide a means of attaching the fan to the foundation. The foundation provides a stable base for the fan. However, the turning gear, coupling, and any controls are not included in the boundary of this component type.

The FMEA process is integrated with other reliability engineering activities, and the effectiveness of the implemented mitigation steps is verified.
